articles.title: Stripe didn’t really buy OpenRouter because of the ‘singularity’
articles.description: What does a payments giant want with a startup that routes prompts between different AI models? Stripe says it's because of "the singularity" but it's really for a far more real and powerful reason.
articles.summary: Stripe invested in OpenRouter due to its capability to route prompts between AI models, not because of the concept of the 'singularity'.
points: Stripe's interest in OpenRouter relates to its ability to improve the workflow of AI models by routing prompts between them.
The company did not mention the concept of the 'singularity' as a motivation for the acquisition.
The acquisition aims to enhance the efficiency of AI development, indicating a focus on practical applications over speculative concepts.
articles.insight: The acquisition of OpenRouter by Stripe suggests an industry trend towards integrating AI-driven workflows for practical efficiency, rather than focusing on speculative future technologies like the 'singularity'.

articles.title: Travis Kalanick kicks off another round of VC bashing: ‘1% are helpful’
articles.description: After raising $1.7 billion for his new robotics company Atoms, Travis Kalanick is introspective about the role VCs have played in his career.
articles.summary: After raising significant funds for Atoms, Travis Kalanick reflects on his past experiences with venture capitalists, acknowledging that only a small fraction have been helpful, while the rest have been largely unhelpful and at times destructive to the technology industry.
points: Travis Kalanick has had a contentious relationship with venture capitalists (VCs), as evidenced by his criticism of the VC industry after raising $1.7 billion for his new robotics company Atoms.
Kalanick specifically cites negative experiences with some VCs, including their destructive behavior towards the industry and his personal company.
Despite his criticisms, Kalanick has also recognized some VCs as helpful, but only a minority, implying that the majority of VCs have been unhelpful or even harmful to the technology sector.
articles.insight: Kalanick's criticism of the VC industry highlights the growing dissatisfaction among founders and entrepreneurs regarding the role of venture capitalists in the technology industry. This could indicate a need for change within the venture capital sector.

points: Rillet, specializing in account creation and management, has attracted $100 million in a Series C funding round.
The company' extruded its ARR (Account Recurring Revenue) by double in the past three months, hinting at strong growth.
Rillet, which emerged from stealth mode two years ago, is now valued at $1 billion, becoming a unicorn.
articles.insight: Rillet's rapid growth and successful funding round indicate a significant opportunity within the account-based solutions space in the financial technology sector.
